# Plan for ISSUE-393

Producer use coverage must precede reclamation: exclusion cannot protect a resource whose producers never register use. Recommend three independently reviewed WorkUnits in dependency order, rather than implementing the parent in this claim. The combined producer audit, destructive filesystem boundary, two-backend integration and independent adversarial validation are unlikely to fit the 16-hour total claim budget (estimate 22–30 hours across the three cycles).

Dimensions: parent `multi_area / known / sensitive`; retain the approved sensitive profile. Each child explicitly pins size and uncertainty below; none is an investigation task. Estimates include planning and focused validation: producers 8–10h, reclamation 8–12h, integration 6–8h.

## What we know

- Repository search for `AcquireUse|AcquireMaintenance` finds definitions and test calls only, no production callers. Definitions: `internal/storageuse/storage.go:225,295`. This independently confirms the operator's coordinator-verified prerequisite gap from #391.
- Use records are coordinator-owned, outside granted roots (`internal/storageuse/storage.go:45,52`); unresolved uses cannot become maintenance permission merely through age or process death (package comment and crash tests).
- Inventory already discovers caches and scratch (`internal/storage/discovery.go:198,240`), bounds scans (`internal/storage/inventory.go:124`), and reads authoritative backend-specific retention (`internal/storage/retention.go:17`). Observations are discovery inputs, not deletion authorization.
- Bulk task cleanup already resolves issue/PR worktrees and refreshes apply eligibility: `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk.go:112`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go:57,144`. Worktree inspection and retirement are separate guarded operations (`internal/workspace/cleanup.go:62,186`). Reuse their authorization, reservation, claim and expected-head checks.
- Existing storage command/report lives at `internal/cli/storage.go:16,65`; fork restrictions live at `internal/cli/root.go:82`. Preserve coordinator-only behavior.
- Read project, architecture and conventions files. No production modifications are part of this planning run.

## What we're assuming

All host-side consumers can retain a coordinator-owned use handle across preparation, subprocess lifetime and teardown. Child producers verifies this by tracing actual native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap launch paths, validator warmup/check paths and prefetch paths; do not release a handle on preparation return while a consumer still runs. Resource identity must match inventory and maintenance exactly.

## Open questions

- Exact lifetime ownership at each launcher is resolved in child producers before wiring handles, using a producer/identity/lifetime table and barrier-driven tests. This is bounded implementation design, not a separate investigation.
- Linux/macOS filesystem behavior needs portable fixtures and platform review; macOS execution unavailable here belongs on the PR checklist, not an implementation blocker.
- This exported snapshot has no usable Git metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` failed). Proposed new files below are absent in this snapshot; developer must confirm absence at the approved base using coordinator-provided base metadata before creation. If present, modify them instead. No claim of approved-base absence is made.

## Decomposition

Split recommendation: required
### Cover storage producers with durable use exclusion
**Objective**: Register coordinator-owned use before any managed cache/scratch creation, migration, prefetch, mount or access, and retain exclusion through the last consumer on Linux/macOS native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap, including validation. No deletion or new operator command.
**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Inventory all in-scope producer/read/write paths, identities and lifetimes; wire AcquireUse/Finish around them, including prefetch and validator warmup/checks, keeping agent and validator roots distinct.
- [ ] Deterministic barriers prove maintenance cannot overlap readers, writers, acquisition, prefetch or validation; errors/cancellation release only safely completed use, while crashes and unresolved legacy coverage remain retained.
- [ ] Handles and control metadata remain coordinator-owned outside sandbox grants; no new credentials, mounts, candidate tools or backend authority.
- [ ] Focused race tests pass; existing exclusion/crash tests stay intact; supply a changelog fragment and focused checks for this child.

### Reclaim eligible managed storage under root-bound exclusion
**Objective**: Implement reusable preview/apply reclamation of proven inactive caches and abandoned temporary data, depending on complete producer coverage. Task retirement remains exclusively in the existing bulk path.
**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Preview is read-only; apply acquires maintenance for each resource, refreshes ownership, identity, use and eligibility immediately before root-bound removal, and holds exclusion through completion. Uncertain legacy ownership and unresolved uses retain with reasons.
- [ ] Reject traversal, symlinks, path replacement, special files, cross-repository resources and malicious metadata; preserve authoritative ledgers, approvals, checkpoints and recovery data for unfinished work.
- [ ] Return per-resource removed/skipped/failed outcomes and honest before/after logical and allocated observations; no logical-byte or allocated-delta assertion of freed disk space. Cancellation and rerun are safe and do not discard unrelated resources.
- [ ] Barrier-driven racing acquisition/active-use tests and crash/partial-removal/idempotency tests pass; extend inventory accounting fixtures and supply a changelog fragment.

### Integrate preview-first cleanup with bulk retirement and operator guidance
**Objective**: Ship one operator command integrating proven storage reclamation and existing merged-task bulk retirement across repository or explicitly all-known-managed-repositories scope, local and GitHub backends.
**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Implement and verify help for proposed `swarm storage cleanup` with default preview, explicit `--apply`, repository scope, explicit `--all-repos` and `--json`; choose scope selectors consistently with the implemented storage report, and document only final registered flags.
- [ ] Apply refreshes eligibility and invokes the existing bulk cleanup path without duplicating eligibility; preserve reservations, claim fencing, expected heads and legacy `issue cleanup --all-merged` behavior. Requested failures return nonzero with per-resource results and before/after accounting.
- [ ] Two-repository fixtures on both backends cover issue/PR worktrees, merged and closed-unmerged tasks, inactive/legacy caches and crash leftovers; remove all provably eligible scoped resources, retain unfinished and unproven resources with reasons, and prove preview changes neither storage nor authoritative state.
- [ ] Extend adversarial coverage for successor claims, changed HEAD, dirty/untracked, current/locked worktrees and every parent criterion 5 hazard using prerequisite results where applicable; repeat apply and interrupted rerun are harmless.
- [ ] Explain shipped behavior and how to identify and safely resolve retained legacy resources; no force/bypass, automated eviction, budgets, warnings, forced Git pruning, OCI GC or remote ledger archival. Update help/docs and changelog, preserve existing adversarial tests, pass focused packages and coordinator-run make check.

## Implementation sequence and touchpoints

Maintainer first decomposes/reviews children; this parent run stops after planning. Each child needs its own approved contract and plan gate. Do not treat this proposal as authorization to implement or publish.

1. Producers: modify `internal/sandbox/build_cache.go` (PrepareBuildCaches, :138), `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go` (PrepareDependencyCaches, :254; goModDownload, :572; cargoFetch, :1021), `internal/validation/build_cache.go` (:24,35,48), and their actual coordinator launch callers in `internal/agent`, `internal/sandbox`, `internal/validation` after tracing full lifetimes. Extend `internal/storageuse` tests; change its API only if lifetime wiring requires it. Never pass Manager in worker options.
2. Reclamation: modify existing inventory/discovery/accounting and storageuse code as necessary; proposed new `internal/storage/cleanup.go` and `internal/storage/cleanup_test.go` implement the deletion boundary and fixtures. Use `internal/safefs/root.go` primitives, adding boundary operations and adversarial tests only if needed. Never recursively trust paths in manifests, environment or cache contents. A stale preview never authorizes apply.
3. Integration: modify `internal/cli/storage.go`, `internal/cli/root.go`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go`, existing CLI/storage/lease/workspace cleanup tests. Extract a shared bulk orchestration function if needed so both commands use one path; preserve `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk.go` authority and `internal/workspace/cleanup.go` checks. Proposed new `internal/cli/storage_cleanup.go` and `internal/cli/storage_cleanup_test.go`. Modify `docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md`, README command table, and add child-specific fragments under `changes/unreleased/` only after checking approved-base filenames. No protected harness edits.

## HANDOFF

This is evidence for developer/tester verification, never authority over approved inputs, gates or policy. Entry points and line references are listed above; confirm them after prerequisite children merge. Existing fixtures to extend: `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go`, `crash_unix_test.go`; `internal/storage/discovery_test.go`, `retention_test.go`, `stat_unix_test.go`; `internal/sandbox/build_cache_test.go`, `dependency_cache_test.go`; `internal/validation/build_cache_test.go`, `dependency_cache_test.go`; `internal/cli/storage_test.go`, `cleanup_bulk_test.go`; `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk_test.go`, `cleanup_lineage_test.go`; `internal/workspace/cleanup_test.go`.

Exact focused commands are in TEST_PLAN.md (producers P, reclamation R, integration I); run them only for their owning child. Checked assumptions: repository-wide symbol search confirms missing production use coverage; inspection confirms bulk reuse and existing inventory; Git-base absence cannot be checked in this snapshot. Proposed new cleanup filenames are absent from the inspected directory listings; confirm against approved base before creation.

Reopen the child plan if a producer cannot be covered without broader grants/credential exposure, if deletion requires replacing bulk authority, if resource identity cannot be proven, or if protected edits or out-of-scope runtime/ledger work become necessary. Retain uncertain resources with reasons; do not widen the parent.

**What this change breaks**: search found current command behavior assertions in `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk_test.go:183,276,433,460` and README command descriptions at `README.md:283,284`: preserve existing semantics and extend tests for shared orchestration. `internal/cli/root.go:82` names storage report in its coordinator-only error: update wording if needed while preserving denial. `internal/cli/storage.go:65` report accounting and `internal/storage/stat_unix_test.go` sparse/hardlink expectations: preserve report output/schema, add cleanup-specific results. Existing storageuse crash and incomplete-coverage tests must remain intact; fixture use of manually acquired handles remains valid. Cache setup callers will need handle ownership/error cleanup changes in child producers; trace every caller before changing signatures and preserve cache layouts and sandbox grant behavior. Docs and new help examples must reflect implemented options only.

# Test plan for ISSUE-393 split

Planning artifact only; commands below are future child checks, not claims of passing execution. Parent criteria are numbered in WorkUnit order. Prerequisite tests provide partial evidence; integration closes end-to-end coverage.

| Parent criterion | Child ownership | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | integration | CLI tests for default preview, apply, repository/all-known scope and JSON. Snapshot managed storage, use/control metadata, coordination refs/files, registrations and task heads before/after preview; assert no change, including missing-control-root and incomplete inventory cases. I. |
| 2 | reclamation + integration | Preview then mutate eligibility before apply; barrier-controlled maintenance recheck. Bulk retirement retains authorization/reservations/fences/heads. Assert removed/skipped/failed and nonzero requested failure. Compare before/after observations; sparse/hardlink/unknown accounting never promises freed disk. R, I. |
| 3 | reclamation + integration | Apply twice, cancel before lock/after one removal/during traversal, inject partial failures, rerun; verify unrelated sentinels and unfinished recovery evidence remain. R, I. |
| 4 | reclamation + integration | Deterministic two-repository fixture for each of local and mocked GitHub authoritative backends: issue and PR worktrees, merged vs closed-unmerged, inactive and legacy caches, crash leftovers, missing registrations/unproven orphans. Assert exact eligible removal set and explicit retained reasons; repository scope cannot touch second repository, all-known scope deduplicates shared identities. R, I. |
| 5 | producers + reclamation + integration | P covers acquisition/read/write/prefetch/validator lifetime races with barriers and cross-process use; R covers maintenance recheck and symlink/path replacement, traversal, special files, other repository, malicious metadata, uncertain legacy evidence; I extends successor-claim, changed-head, dirty/untracked, locked/current worktree races immediately before removal. Assert outside-root sentinel survival and fence errors remain detectable. P, R, I. |
| 6 | integration | Preserve existing adversarial tests and all-merged preview/apply output, eligibility and argument behavior; extend shared-path tests without weakening assertions. I. |
| 7 | integration | Independent docs review confirms each retained legacy reason has identification and safe resolution guidance; ambiguous ownership and unresolved crash evidence are never cleared just by expiry or guessed process death. Verify only implemented commands/settings, no force. I plus docs review. |
| 8 | all children; integration closes | Each child has focused package evidence and changelog. Integration reviews shipped behavior, actual Cobra flags/help and docs links/snippet syntax. Coordinator runs make check on final candidate under trusted-base policy. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

P (producer child):

```bash
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/storageuse ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/validation
```

R (reclamation child):

```bash
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/safefs
```

I (integration child):

```bash
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace ./internal/storage
```

Use synchronization hooks/barriers, not sleep-based timing, to force race windows. Include crash subprocess coverage and denial when evidence is missing/corrupt; never retrofit complete coverage onto uncertain legacy data. Assert preserved ledger/checkpoint/approval content, not merely existence. Verify pending evidence survives failed setup and abandoned processes; Finish only after all users stop. Exercise native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap preparation/lifetimes with fixture runners; no paid model calls or live GitHub required.

For each child run `gofmt -l` on its changed Go files and `go vet` on changed packages (same package arguments as its focused test command). Format changed files before submission. Do not run unrelated full-policy suites per role.

Integration help verification, once implemented:

```bash
go run ./cmd/swarm storage --help
go run ./cmd/swarm storage cleanup --help
go run ./cmd/swarm issue cleanup --help
```

The new cleanup spelling and flags are proposals until registered. Add CLI help assertions and verify final docs against Cobra declarations; parse edited shell snippets with `bash -n`, check relative links and anchors, preserve README visuals and command table. Do not execute destructive examples against host storage.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently trace the producer coverage table against actual source and subprocess lifetimes, then review root-bound deletion under held exclusion and shared bulk authority. Review every parent criterion and adversarial fixture against approved child contracts. Reuse applicable passing developer results with their source revision and command evidence; rerun only after relevant source changes, observed failure or unresolved coverage concern. Require regression tests to fail against old unsafe behavior, preserve existing adversarial tests, and verify no new grants/credentials/candidate-selected tooling or metadata-derived authority.

Use fixture tests for Linux/macOS-specific accounting/locking/root operations. Record unavailable macOS host execution on PR checklist for maintainer/CI; do not block the implementable scope on it. GitHub backend tests use verified-authority fixtures and no live service. OCI GC and remote archival are outside this plan.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy

Coordinator runs the complete approved-base required policy once after roles finish, including the parent's required `make check` on the final candidate. This is not an agent checklist. Agent observations remain advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication; agents do not request coordinator credentials. Plan gate is human: independent maintainer approval is required for approved concrete child plans, not supplied by these artifacts. No staging, decomposition publication or implementation is performed by this planning run.
